setupSteps: Set the pulley high. Place the pulley at about forehead height, or slightly above (sources say eye level to just above the head; too low turns it into an upright row, too high encourages shrugging).
Attach the rope. Clip a rope attachment to the carabiner; check it is locked.
Choose a very light weight. Use the lightest plate or one of the lightest. Machine plate weights vary and are not standardised; choose a load that lets you pause at the end for 1-2 seconds.

Grip the rope. Hold one end in each hand with the thumbs pointing toward you (back toward your face) and the palms facing each other. Some sources call this neutral, others overhand; FitPlate uses the thumbs-toward-you description.
Step back to set tension. Walk back until the cable is taut with your arms straight in front of you at about eye height. Stand with feet hip-width, one foot slightly forward if you like, knees soft.
Brace. Ribs down, abdominals tight, chest tall, shoulders gently down away from the ears. Optional: half-kneel if you tend to lean back (Muscle & Strength suggestion).
Check the view. For the camera or mirror, stand square to the stack so both elbows are visible.
Anchor the band at about eye to forehead height on a door anchor (door closing away from you), a rack upright or a sturdy post; check it before every set.
Hold one end in each hand, step back until the band has light tension and follow the same steps as the cable version.

steps.title: Take the rope and step back
steps.action: Grip the rope with thumbs toward you, step back until the cable is tight, arms straight at about eye height.
steps.feel: Light stretch across the shoulder blades.
steps.visualCheck: Front: both arms straight toward the pulley at the same height; side: ears over shoulders, ribs down.

steps.title: Set the shoulders
steps.action: Draw the shoulders gently down and back without leaning.

steps.title: Start the pull with the elbows
steps.action: Bend the elbows and pull the rope toward your face, leading with the elbows out wide and high.
steps.visualCheck: Front: elbows at about shoulder height or just below, wider than the wrists; not tucked to the ribs.

steps.title: Pull the ends apart
steps.action: As the rope nears your face, split your hands apart so they move toward your ears.
steps.feel: Outer shoulder blade area, the rotator cuff, working.
steps.visualCheck: Front: hands separate and end beside the ears.

steps.title: Rotate and finish
steps.action: Turn the forearms upward so the hands finish beside the ears, upper arm and forearm forming about a 90-degree angle (est.; sources describe roughly 90 degrees).
steps.visualCheck: Front: elbows high, hands beside ears, wrists not bent back; side: trunk upright, no lean.

steps.title: Squeeze and pause
steps.action: Squeeze the shoulder blades together for 1-2 seconds without shrugging.
steps.feel: Strong squeeze between the shoulder blades.
steps.breathing: Hold the breath only briefly; do not strain.
steps.visualCheck: Front: no rise of the shoulders toward the ears; side: no lean.

steps.title: Return under control
steps.action: Slowly extend the arms back to the start, keeping elbows high until the arms are nearly straight.
steps.visualCheck: Front: both arms return together; the stack does not slam.

steps.title: Reset
steps.action: Pause with the cable taut (do not let the stack rest), then repeat.
steps.visualCheck: Front: shoulders still low; side: ribs still down.

commonMistakes.title: Using too heavy a weight
commonMistakes.text: Using too heavy a weight. Why: form breaks, you lean back and yank. Fix: drop the weight until you can pause 1-2 seconds at the finish every rep (several sources call this the most common mistake).

commonMistakes.title: Leaning back
commonMistakes.text: Leaning back. Why: the lower back and hips take over and the shoulders get little work. Fix: step closer, lighten the load, stagger your stance or half-kneel.

commonMistakes.title: Shrugging
commonMistakes.text: Shrugging. Why: the upper trapezius takes over from the rear shoulder. Fix: keep the shoulders down and think "hands apart" rather than "pull up".

commonMistakes.title: Letting the elbows drop
commonMistakes.text: Letting the elbows drop. Why: it becomes a high row and loses the rotation. Fix: keep the elbows at about shoulder height or just below, wider than the hands.

commonMistakes.title: Pulling to the nose with no hand separation
commonMistakes.text: Pulling to the nose with no hand separation. Why: no external rotation, the move becomes a rope curl or row. Fix: split the rope ends apart as they near the face and finish beside the ears.

commonMistakes.title: Pulley too low or too high
commonMistakes.text: Pulley too low or too high. Why: too low gives an upright-row pattern, too high encourages shrugging. Fix: set about eye to forehead height.

commonMistakes.title: Letting the weight stack slam
commonMistakes.text: Letting the weight stack slam. Why: it jerks the shoulder and loses control. Fix: return in 2-3 seconds and do not rest the stack between reps.

commonMistakes.title: Wrist bent back at the end
commonMistakes.text: Wrist bent back at the end. Why: puts strain on the wrist. Fix: keep the wrist in line with the forearm and loosen the grip.

safetyNotes: Keep the load light. The face pull is not a heavy lift. If you lean back or shrug to finish, the weight is too heavy.

Shoulder pain: no trial of face pulls in shoulder impingement was found. Related review evidence suggests external-rotator and shoulder-blade work is a common part of rehab, but it needs to match symptoms. Keep the pull pain-free; stop with sharp or pinching pain.
High blood pressure: avoid long breath-holding; stop 2-3 reps before failure.

Cable station: check the rope is locked on, do not walk away with the stack raised, return the rope gently, and keep others clear of the rope path. Band at home: inspect the band for nicks, use a secure anchor on a door that closes away from you, and never let go of the band while stretched.
Gym etiquette: re-rack the rope, wipe the handles, do not film other members, do not hog the cable station during long rests.

The angle thresholds (150, 100 and 70 degrees), the lean limit (10 degrees), the shrug threshold (15 percent), the 2 s minimum rep, the pulley height, and all sets, reps and rest values are FitPlate choices (est.), not validated. Not found: an ACE, NSCA, Harvard Health, NHS or Mayo Clinic face pull page; the ExRx face pull page; an EMG study of the rope face pull itself; a controlled study of face pulls for desk-posture or impingement outcomes; a face-pull-specific professional-body prescription or Compendium code; a validated starting load; a validated pulley height; condition-specific sources for knee pain, lower back pain, obesity and PCOS; the primary ACOG page.

conditionCautions.change: No long breath-holding; stop 2-3 reps before failure; no lifting if resting BP >= 180/120; uncontrolled BP: ask a doctor

conditionCautions.change: 2-3 non-consecutive resistance days per week; usual glucose checks if on insulin or sulfonylureas
conditionCautions.source: ADA position statement, Colberg et al. 2016

conditionCautions.change: After clearance: light loads, continuous breathing, no straining; arm work at or above chest height can raise blood pressure more
conditionCautions.source: AHA resistance exercise statement (via ACC summary 2023)

conditionCautions.change: Part of 2+ days per week resistance work with aerobic activity
Light exercise; half-kneel or seated variant if standing balance is a worry; exercise-specific advice not found
conditionCautions.source: ACSM weight management position stand (Donnelly et al. 2009)

conditionCautions.change: Fits muscle-strengthening guidance; exercise-specific advice not found
Train normally if controlled; start at beginner level with ongoing fatigue
Warm up and keep reliever inhaler nearby
Standing loads the knees little; seated or half-kneeling version if standing is painful; condition-specific source not found
Staggered stance or half-kneeling to avoid leaning back; tall still trunk and light load; acute pain or disc problems: ask a professional; condition-specific source not found
Lighter load, smaller range, elbows no higher than shoulder height, stop before pinching; pain over 2 weeks, night pain, weakness or catching: see a clinician
